state: We need experimental job definitions before implementation planning, with four future checks and no runs today. Ordinary Can functions must eventually own all scenario logic and expectations; agent authors are the intended audience. The agreed system assigns judgment to qualified R, subjects to C and resource management to a separate Go N. No accepted R/N program or Can live-probe entry is available, so preliminary host-measured results must remain design evidence and cannot accept tools, replace coverage or remove existing harnesses. Local inventory includes the pinned Bun 1.4.2, Python 3.14.7 supporting os.posix_spawn descriptor mappings, Go 1.27.1 and Playwright 1.55.1, but no materialized Can compiler. The 256 GB laptop requires small disk/load budgets; large builds, installations and performance work are on hold. Each proposed check names one uncertainty, raw or fixed independent measurements, a fault injection, an end-to-end time cap and an external resource owner. A minimal Python host process could register a controlled child graph before launching, deliver fd 3 JSON separately from fd 0 binary data, retain kill/wait authority and reclaim marked scratch after success, failure or handled interruption. Its conclusion would cover POSIX/Bun descriptor mechanics, excluding Go ExtraFiles/product-launcher correctness, owner-death recovery and arbitrary detached descendants. Alternatively a small compiled Go parent would exercise os.Pipe with exec.Cmd.ExtraFiles at the cost of a stdlib build and explicit build-cache budget. Implementing the complete N would be a larger prerequisite. The native transport proposal PM-N1 refers to a then-getter object only through integer IDs. For PM-N2 the existing runtime/codec/json.ts::encodeJSON export accepts a minimal schema for an int array; a hostile own-index accessor should yield type with an empty path and no getter executions. An independently checked count changes under an intentional index-read shim. This source-level call cannot establish C-generated ordinary Can ingress, emitted state wiring or an R verdict. Those integrated N2 requirements retain a C output identity, typed same-realm seam, invocation evidence and accepted R/N. Producing C now broadens the experiment beyond direct-module mechanics, while waiting until integration leaves this narrower empirical question open. Browser preparation uses a paused form-navigation POST, direct observation of Playwright click settlement and a route response chosen in another process; premature click completion is recorded as inconclusive. Database work is excluded. All four proposals are still unrun.

temporary_owner.instructions: What supervision setup should these preliminary jobs start with under the stated constraints?

criteria.python_scoped: Start with the small Python instrument and record its bounded authority; postpone claims about Go integration, parent death and complete N.
criteria.go_small: Use a tiny compiled Go instrument first, budgeting compilation resources in exchange for directly exercising the product-style pipe mapping.
criteria.full_owner: Make the finished Go resource service a prerequisite for starting this exploratory work.

source_ingress.instructions: How should this preparation address hostile-value access to candidate code?

criteria.source_partial: Use the small source-import experiment to inform ingress design without claiming the later Can artifact integration.
criteria.compiled_now: Require the compiled Can boundary in the immediate experiment, including candidate build and typed access implementation.
criteria.defer: Retain only the source analysis for now and schedule every ingress run after C integration becomes available.
